title: [Core] Speed up decode by remove synchronizing operation in sampler (#16436)

workload.note: Removes CUDA sync in apply_penalties; win via GPU serving + trace. ~8% decode for small models.

policy.one_run_is: one `docker run` of the workload cmd per arm per repeat (same image, arm tree swapped in by the prelude)

contention_gate.rules: wait while another tenant uses the GPU (>5 % util or a foreign compute process >1 GiB) or the CPU (load1 > nproc/2)

policy.machine_snapshot: machine.py snapshot per workload run -> data/pr_<n>/work/machine_<arm>_<i>.json

arm_isolation.tree: wipe the wheel's vllm/*.py, copy the arm's vllm/ over site-packages (compiled .so stay)
arm_isolation.files: overlay ONLY task.json:source_files from the arm over the wheel's own tree
arm_isolation.tests_benchmarks: copied from the PR's merge tree to /t without a sibling vllm/ package

policy.noise_model: measure.py: paired log-speedup, MAD sigma, theta = clip(k*sigma, theta_min, theta_max) with k/theta from config.yaml:measure

reported.gain_evidence: By refactoring the code to avoid the indexing, we can remove the sync and allow much more of the sampling phase CPU work to overlap with the forward pass on the

author_hardware_args.text: By refactoring the code to avoid the indexing, we can remove the sync and allow much more of the sampling phase CPU work to overlap with the forward pass on the GPU, providing an 8% speedup to decoding for smaller models.
VLLM_FLASH_ATTN_VERSION=3 VLLM_USE_V1=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct --enable-prefix-caching --dtype float16 --disable-log-requests -O3

hardware.gpu_hint: serving bench: needs a vllm server + client

standalone.run_baseline: docker run --rm --gpus device=0 --shm-size=2g -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 -e CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID -e HF_HUB_DISABLE_PROGRESS_BARS=1 -v $PWD/data/pr_16436:/task:ro -v $PWD/.weights/hf:/root/.cache/huggingface -e ARM=baseline vllm-task:16436 -lc 'A=/base; site=$(python3 -c "import vllm,os;print(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(vllm.__file__)))"); find "$site/vllm" -name "*.py" -delete; cp -a $A/vllm/. "$site/vllm/"; ln -sfn $A /src; rm -rf /t && mkdir -p /t && cd /gold && for d in tests benchmarks pyproject.toml conftest.py; do [ -e "$d" ] && cp -a "$d" /t/; done; cd /t; python3 benchmarks/benchmark_serving.py --backend vllm --model facebook/opt-125m --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1000 --random-output-len 100 --num-prompts 100'
standalone.run_pr_solution: docker run --rm --gpus device=0 --shm-size=2g -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 -e CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID -e HF_HUB_DISABLE_PROGRESS_BARS=1 -v $PWD/data/pr_16436:/task:ro -v $PWD/.weights/hf:/root/.cache/huggingface -e ARM=pr_solution vllm-task:16436 -lc 'A=/gold; site=$(python3 -c "import vllm,os;print(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(vllm.__file__)))"); find "$site/vllm" -name "*.py" -delete; cp -a $A/vllm/. "$site/vllm/"; ln -sfn $A /src; rm -rf /t && mkdir -p /t && cd /gold && for d in tests benchmarks pyproject.toml conftest.py; do [ -e "$d" ] && cp -a "$d" /t/; done; cd /t; python3 benchmarks/benchmark_serving.py --backend vllm --model facebook/opt-125m --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1000 --random-output-len 100 --num-prompts 100'
standalone.note: The image already holds both trees (/base = baseline commit, /gold = the PR's merge commit); the one-liner swaps the chosen tree over the installed wheel exactly like run_one.sh's prelude, then runs the workload cmd from /t (the merge tree's tests/ + benchmarks/). NOT PINNED: task.json has no `wheel` yet, so the Dockerfile installs the latest PyPI vLLM (compiled ops may not match either tree) and run_one.sh refuses to run it. `python3 gen/gen_tasks.py <pr>` picks the first PyPI release after merge_sha.
